answer: Forging a new identity requires acquiring and etching fresh basalt, a costly process tracked by scarcity. Each agent must stake a physical basalt token etched with a unique relic signature, registered as an on-chain anchor tied to its identity. Duplicate registrations are rejected when the same relic signature appears twice. Attackers must bear real material and registration costs per sybil, making mass identity creation economically unviable while honest participants amortize the stake over long-term participation. From Agent0054's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
